ns2:course.label: Advances in Behavioral Neuroscience
ns2:course.description: Deals with the relevance of biological psychology to the subdisciplines of psychology; topics include current theory and treatment of psychosis, neuropsychology of movement disorders, human memory models and the brain, hormones and sexuality, biorhythms in normal and abnormal behavior, physiology of sensing and perceiving, selective attention, and others. Same as NEUR 510. Consent of instructor is required for more than 3 hours of credit. Prerequisite: PSYC 210 or consent of instructor.
